# Best 18650 chargers

**Best overall: XTAR VC4SL, about $32.90**
- It has four independent bays, USB-C with QC3.0 input, and adjustable current from 0.25A to 3A.
- Its LCD shows voltage, current, capacity and internal resistance per cell. It also has capacity-grading and storage modes.
- It fits cells from 10440 to 32650, including protected 21700s, and also charges NiMH/NiCd.
- Best Batteries rated it 4.3/5. VoltRated recommends it for anyone with 18650/21700 cells.
- Drawbacks:
  - One reviewer says it defaults to the highest current, so press the Curr button and pick 500mA-1A for everyday charging.
  - The same reviewer saw it end NiMH charges early and occasionally mistake a NiMH cell for Li-ion, so watch the start of a NiMH charge.
  - It doesn't list LiFePO4 support.
- Buy and price details: [Best Batteries listing](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/). Reviews: [1Lumen](https://1lumen.com/battery-charger-review/xtar-vc4sl/), [Stephen Knight](https://www.stephenknightphotography.com/post/charger-review-xtar-vc4sl).

**Best for speed or LiFePO4: Nitecore UMS4, about $38.95**
- It charges up to 3A in a single slot (1A each with all four filled).
- It supports Li-ion, IMR, LiFePO4 and NiMH, and has reverse-polarity, short-circuit and overtime protection.
- It also shows internal resistance and has a Li-ion restoration mode.
- Product page: [Nitecore](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4). Price reference: [Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/).

**Budget pick: Tenergy TN270, $18.99**
- It's a simple two-bay wall charger with reverse-polarity detection.
- It charges at only 500mA per slot, so a 3,000 mAh cell takes about 6-7 hours. It has no USB input and takes 18650, 18500 and 14500 cells only.
- It has a 12-month warranty and 30-day returns.
- [Buy at Tenergy](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.

**Other option:** Smashing Robotics ranks the Keenstone 4-Bay Universal Charger first, citing a 4.6-star average across 4,608 reviews, selectable 500mA/1A charging and UL/CE/FCC certification. It also ranks the IMREN 2-Bay USB-C as a travel pick. I don't have direct purchase links for those, but the [review is here](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/).

**Safety tips**
- Choose a charger with independent bays and a clear Li-ion cutoff (4.2V). VoltRated advises avoiding no-name units that don't say how they end a charge.
- Charge at 0.5A-1A when you're not in a hurry, since slower charging is easier on the cell.
- Don't leave cells in the charger for days.

I'd go with the VC4SL unless you need LiFePO4, in which case get the UMS4. Prices are as listed by the sources and may have changed.
